_what: The permission each account must hold on each CODE repository (#3124; ADR 0039, item 7, under #69). Keys starting with an underscore are prose and are not read. `docs/repository-access.md` says what the model is and who may edit GitHub to match it; `packages/lab/src/packaging/layer-repository-access.test.ts` pins this file and, behind `A11Y_CHECK_REPO_ACCESS=1`, `layer-repository-access-live.test.ts` reads `repos/<r>/collaborators` back and names every difference.
_repositories: Every `repo` of `.agent-org/project.json`'s `code` array, plus `a11ign/screenreader-worker`, which exists (public, created empty 2026-09-26) and is not in that array until #2701 moves code into it. A test pins the key set equal to that union, so a repository added to `code` without a row here is red.
_roles: `admin`, `write`, `read` and `none`. `none` means NO direct collaborator grant: the account may still read a public repository, and holds nothing it could be asked to lose. The names are GitHub's own `role_name` values, so the live read compares them as strings.
_agentsNeverAdmin: No agent account is `admin` anywhere. An agent with admin can edit the ruleset and classic protection of the repository whose review requirement `main-review-requirement.md` says nobody may walk past, and the admin-only `branches/main/protection` read then answers as that agent: the two families of access (read the protection, be exempt from it) collapse. ADR 0039, item 7.
_bots: The `bots` org team is attached to the layer repositories and is the route by which the agent accounts reach them. Its level on a layer is `push` (write), never `admin`. At the time of filing (2026-10-03) it holds `admin` on `a11ign/screenreader-worker`, which is the one difference from this file; the downgrade is an org-admin act (the chairman's) and is NOT performed by the row that wrote this file.
